title: Hosted Eve Runtime Qualification And Durable Handoff Tasks

harnessContract.acceptedOutcome: The exact custom-channel route returns 202 only after Eve-owned Workflow start or intended-session hook-resume acceptance, then Preview directly proves the matching durable session and turn resume without a second app Workflow.
stopConditions: Stop on source, lock, Eve reference, config, deployment, function, duration, provider, authority, rollback, or observation-epoch mismatch.
Stop if implementation adds a second app-level Workflow or raw Workflow client without a new pinned-source finding that proves a missing Eve boundary.
Stop if 202 can precede the awaited Eve send acceptance identity.
Stop if an existing-session resume failure falls through to a different new run and that continuity fork is treated as successful acceptance.
Stop on blind retry after an outcome-uncertain provider write.
Stop when a guessed vercel.json glob, patched generated output, Sandbox timeout, local Build Output, or broad suite is offered as hosted function-duration or durability proof.
Stop every hosted/provider operation until the target-owned runbook and one-run authority are attached.

principles: Eve 0.20 owns Workflow start, resume, durable sessions, and per-turn child workflows.
Bundjil owns the provider webhook, replay claim, send acceptance ordering, provider side-effect safety, and evidence.
A 202 response follows awaited Eve send acceptance and intended-session convergence; starting an Effect Fiber, registering waitUntil, or accepting a fallback continuity fork is insufficient.
waitUntil extends only the ordinary webhook invocation up to that function's timeout.
Workflow lifetime, each function or step invocation, Sandbox idle timeout, and session lifetime are separate clocks.
Decode unknown input once at ingress, use canonical Schema Type values internally, and encode at outward boundaries.
Effects stay flat, lazy, linear and typed; raw clients, DTO mirrors, casts, stringly policy, wrappers and helper sprawl are forbidden.
Every hosted consequence is runbook- and authority-gated; repository proof never grants external authority.
riskLenses: Ownership and call graph: provider ingress, replay, EveChannelDispatch, Eve send, Workflow runtime, provider effects and evidence remain distinct.
Effect quality: Schema, branded identities, Config/Redacted, tagged errors, Services/Layers, Scope/Fiber/Exit/Match and direct operations remain canonical.
Boundary and lifecycle correctness: send start/resume acceptance, 202 ordering, waitUntil limit, duplicate convergence, interrupted step replay, uncertainty and rollback.
Verification and adversarial coverage: each acceptance, timeout, retry, duplicate and interruption claim has a direct observable and false-green rejection.
Documentation, authority and closeout: architecture, README, runbooks, authority, verification journeys, immutable packets and lifecycle pointers agree.

auditFindings.summary: Pinned Eve 0.20 already owns durable session and turn workflows through startWorkflowPreferLatest and resumeHook.
auditFindings.rootCorrection: Reuse Eve send and reject a second app-owned Workflow unless future pinned source proves a missing boundary.

auditFindings.summary: Bundjil currently returns 202 while send runs in a background Fiber under waitUntil.
auditFindings.rootCorrection: Move 202 after awaited send acceptance identity and return provider-retryable non-2xx on pre-acceptance rejection or timeout.

auditFindings.summary: waitUntil shares the ordinary webhook function timeout and does not prove cross-process durability.
auditFindings.rootCorrection: Retain Exit observability while using the matching Workflow run as the durable oracle.

auditFindings.summary: Eve deliberately generates the workflow flow function with Node 24, a namespaced queue trigger and maxDuration max.
auditFindings.rootCorrection: Preserve Eve-owned workflow output and read it back from the immutable Preview deployment.

auditFindings.summary: The generated ordinary __server function has no maxDuration; Eve directly owns Nitro creation and exposes no application duration seam in 0.20.
auditFindings.rootCorrection: Measure handoff latency and effective project duration; if an override is justified, use a supported Eve application seam or pinned upstream Eve change and Preview readback.

auditFindings.summary: Workflow replay does not make provider writes exactly once and historical receipts do not prove a newer candidate.
auditFindings.rootCorrection: Directly prove exact-result observation, idempotency or quarantine, same-ID duplicates, new immutable packets and explicit non-claims.

auditFindings.summary: Pinned Eve 0.20 send falls through to starting a new session after any deliver error, not only a no-active-session result.
auditFindings.rootCorrection: For existing continuations, observe intended versus accepted run identity and reject or quarantine a fallback continuity fork before 202.

It imports the redacted Channel secret once, applies domain-separated HMAC inputs, and returns only branded work/session fingerprints plus Schema-owned attempts, acceptance, phase/outcome, timestamp and latency contracts.

EveChannelDispatch keeps the raw Eve Session inside the live adapter, decodes Session.id once with EveSessionId, and returns a safe ChannelHandoffAcceptance after the exact send Promise resolves. The route records Prepared, SendStarted, SendAccepted/SendRejected, Response and native Fiber Exit phases. Exit is preclassified as succeeded, typed failure, defect or interruption before observation, so retained data contains no raw error or Cause and acceptance remains distinct from settlement.

A deterministic delayed-send route fixture records Prepared, SendStarted and Response while send remains pending, then SendAccepted and Exit only after release. Separate fixtures directly prove rejected send, completion defect and runtime-disposal interruption outcomes without changing the current acknowledgement semantics.

tasks.description: Await Eve send acceptance and intended-session convergence before 202, make pre-acceptance failure retryable or quarantined, and preserve replay/uncertainty semantics without adding a Workflow wrapper.

Run Channel/provider/agent focused matrices and repository policy gates.
completionCriteria: 202 follows Eve send acceptance and intended-session convergence in every direct fixture.
Duplicate and uncertain-side-effect properties pass independently.
Implementation is ready for timeout readback and Preview but makes no hosted claim.
completionEvidence: The route now awaits the exact Eve send Promise inside EveChannelDispatch and returns 202 only after a Schema-owned safe acceptance and atomic app-owned continuity convergence. It registers no critical waitUntil work; rejection, timeout, replay/observation failure, interruption, defect or continuity uncertainty produces no 202.

ChannelReplay atomically classifies an ownerless continuation as New, a matching accepted fingerprint as Resumed, and a different accepted fingerprint as ContinuityUncertain. The uncertain claim is retained, exact redelivery is suppressed, matching terminal completion/failure alone retires an owner, and stale terminal settlement cannot clear a newer owner.

The app-owned handoff deadline is decoded through Config.schema as a positive Effect Duration. Its 15-second constants.ts value is a conservative product default below Sendblue's last documented 45-second response deadline, not a provider requirement or hosted latency/function-duration readback. Timeout interrupts the local wait, records a safe timeout, quarantines the claim, returns 503 and never blind-retries the possibly accepted Eve write.

Direct route fixtures separately prove New and Resumed 202 ordering, delayed send withholding 202, one send under a concurrent same-ID duplicate, rejection, handoff timeout, continuity-fork 503, defect, interruption/finalizer and request-abort behavior. The atomic continuity fixture proves deliberate ownerless fallback, matching resume, different-owner quarantine, failed terminal retention, user repair, stale settlement and deliberate post-terminal restart.

Failed terminal state is retained under the same safe session fingerprint used by the SessionTerminal observation. The incident runbook assigns an immediate alert threshold and the next fresh authenticated provider message as the repair route; it forbids payload replay, replay-state clearing, synthesized Eve runs and blind uncertain-write retry.

No provider operation is admitted to Effect.retry in this slice: Sendblue and Photon uncertain transport/write timeouts remain one-attempt readback-required failures, known retryable ingress responses rely on provider redelivery, and a retained uncertain identity suppresses a second effect. The proposed three-attempt/backoff/jitter policy remains unadmitted pending measured operation-specific evidence.

Twenty-eight focused Config/handoff/continuity/route/vertical tests passed; the final full agent suite passed 73 tests after ordinary and Vercel Eve builds; Sendblue passed 9 tests and Photon passed 25 tests. Agent typechecking, Effect language-service setup/diagnostics, boundary, docs, skills, authority, controls, verification-policy, HGI-307, local skill validation, formatting, Knip and diff checks passed in the fresh complete repository verification.

The first full agent-test attempt stopped before tests at the fail-closed missing Executor endpoint. The accepted rerun used only the documented public synthetic build-time endpoint and made no authenticated provider request.

The receipt is repository/local-build proof only. No deployment, provider mutation/readback, webhook, credential, message, Preview, Production, Workflow run, plan limit, Vercel effective duration, hosted alert or durable-resumption claim is established.
